# Historical evidence synthesis: recursive delegation

## Scope and coverage

This audit covers batch 1 of 1 for `hintrsi/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation`: all 35 supplied source inventories and their model-reviewed chunks, not the raw files or linked evaluation artifacts. File counts include copies and teacher records; they are not counts of independent trials. The original task prompt is generally unavailable, so recursive delegation and caller resumption are inferred goals, not a complete specification. Formal counts below are inventory reports; individual evaluator failures and their causes are not supplied.

**Citation paths.** For compactness, let `R` denote `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/`. Unless otherwise noted, cited student sources are `R/codex_parallel_N/lanes/codex_parallel_N_lane0/codex_parallel_N_lane0_G_rK/infer_logs/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/turn_1/trajs.json`, using the indicated N, group G and round K. Teacher sources use the same run and lane prefix, followed by `codex_parallel_N_lane0_G/reviews/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/round_K/teacher/trajs.json`; shared guidance sources instead end in `codex_parallel_N_lane0_shared/hint_gen/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/trajs.json`. H0002 is `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-baseline-run/runs/baseline_ds1017_claudecode_a1_20261120_r1/infer_logs/claude-code-by-agents-recursive-delegation/turn_1/trajs.json`. Event citations refer to `main_agent` unless stated otherwise.

## Evidence matrix

| Sources and role | Observed attempt or stop | Outcome and evidentiary limit |
|---|---|---|
| **H0076** (08/B/1), **H0132** (12/I/2), students | Both made nonempty recursive-delegation changes. H0076’s mock passed and its final diff and commit are visible (events 64–71). H0132 corrected an intermediate request that omitted instruction and image content, then exercised mocked success, errors, unknown targets and cycles (events 49–57, 84–85, 108–111). | Inventory reports **solved**, 7/7 fail-to-pass and 31/31 pass-to-pass for each. Both nevertheless had a local abort-controller assertion failure. H0132 reproduced it after replacing only the handler with its main version—not a complete clean-baseline comparison (events 83, 88, 92–93). Formal success is not universal runtime proof. |
| **H0002**; **H0039** (05/H/1); **H0040** (05/I/1); **H0078** (08/H/1); **H0081** (08/I/1); **H0126** (12/H/1), students | Nonempty changes and selected mocked or type-check validation are visible. H0039’s reproduction changed from one parent call to parent–child–parent calls (events 25–28, 48–50); H0126’s continuation mock passed, but typecheck lacked generated `cli/version.ts` and tests and commit remained outstanding (events 56–62). | H0002 and H0081 report **2/7** fail-to-pass; the others **6/7**. All report **31/31** pass-to-pass and formally not solved. These scores do not identify the defective case. H0002’s same cleanup failure was reproduced on a stashed baseline (events 135–138); that comparison should not be assumed for every similar assertion. |
| **H0065** (07/H/1), **H0079** (08/H/2), students | Both had nonempty edits and pre-change mock failures. H0065’s build hit missing frontend assets; its subsequent chained verification has no visible result (events 24–42). H0079 edited provider-related code, but no handler recursion or post-edit test is visible (events 25–48). | Both ended `incomplete` with `CancelledError`; evaluation is **missing**, so post-edit correctness is unknown. This is interruption, not an empty patch or a proven algorithmic failure. |
| **H0120–H0122** (12/B/1–3), **H0128** (12/H/3), **H0131** (12/I/1), **H0136–H0137** (12/M/2–3), students | Inventory records zero-byte patches. H0121 created a branch and its mock showed only a parent call (events 10, 14, 33–35); H0122 and H0128 inspected and branched without visible implementation (H0122 events 10–14, 27; H0128 events 15, 20, 25). H0136 stated a read-only restriction, but metadata records no denial (event 7; top-level metadata). | Each is reported **0/7** fail-to-pass, **31/31** pass-to-pass, formally not solved. These are not tests of a newly implemented algorithm. A branch is not a fix; a claimed permission restriction is not an observed denial. |
| **H0127** (12/H/2), student | Branch and temporary reproduction existed; the mock exited 1 without worker execution or continuation (events 35–39). The student requested provider-scope clarification and reported no fix or commit (event 40). | Its 1,776-byte patch is **not empty**, although its complete contents are not supplied. Inventory reports 0/7 and 31/31, not solved. The mock establishes a baseline failure in that setup, not failure of an implemented fix. |
| **H0042, H0066, H0083, H0138**, shared teachers (05, 07, 08, 12) | Teachers inspected baseline code and reference diffs, then created guidance artifacts; for example H0138 events 3, 12–14 and 24–25. | A reference diff was inspected, not applied. Successful guidance-file creation is not implementation or acceptance; student receipt and use are not shown. |
| **H0038, H0041, H0077, H0080, H0082, H0123–H0125, H0129–H0130, H0133–H0135**, review teachers | Reviews created review artifacts and reported student actions or diagnoses, e.g. H0038 events 3–5; H0134 events 3–5. | Reviews are secondary evidence unless corroborated by a student trace. Review completion, blank student-patch fields, and an empty `structuredPatch` in a review-file creation response do not establish student success or an empty student patch. |

## Comparison and constraints

**Successful acceptance versus observed behavior.** H0076 and H0132 are counterexamples to treating every local failure as formal failure: both have reported formal success despite the cleanup assertion. Conversely, H0039 and H0078 achieved narrow before/after call-count improvements but remain formally partial; a parent–child–parent count does not independently establish returned payloads, authorization, live-provider behavior or all recursive cases (H0039 events 25, 48–50; H0078 events 30–35, 58–59). H0040’s mock checked accumulated text, a matching tool ID and cleanup after stream completion, yet its immediate cleanup assertion failed and its formal outcome remained partial (events 39, 42–43). These observations support separating test scope, timing and acceptance rather than attributing a score to a single mechanism.

**Stops are materially different.** H0120 and H0121 actually received a Claude API skill instruction to stop and ask on non-Anthropic markers; their final clarification requests followed inspection, and H0121 explicitly cited the rule (H0120 events 3, 18, 25, 29; H0121 events 3, 11, 22, 35). This supports skill-rule adoption, not teacher-hint adoption. H0137’s question is consistent with that delivered instruction, but causation is not independently established (events 3–6). H0136 instead *reported* a read-only policy without an observed denial. H0002’s Git-history requests were denied, but it later created a branch and implemented changes (events 35–36, 63–64, 71–72, 102–103): a limited permission stop did not terminate the attempt. Wrong executable paths, module formats, duplicate CLI flags and missing generated files were also local obstacles, not interchangeable with permission stops or algorithm defects (H0079 events 27–30; H0040 events 25–27; H0132 events 66–74).

**Advice, diagnosis and adoption.** Available hint paths and online-check counts do not show delivered text. After-round reviews cannot be input to the reviewed round. H0042 and H0138 visibly produced guides, but neither shows student receipt or execution (H0042 events 24–26; H0138 events 24–26). H0038 and H0077 diagnose missing context, request scope or stream attribution and report alignment with earlier guidance; their student operations are reviewer reports, and similarity does not prove reliance (each event 5). H0130 labels guidance used while expressly conceding alignment cannot establish causation (event 5). No supplied student audit establishes teacher-hint receipt and causal adoption; actual skill delivery is a distinct category.

**Task-specific facts and hypotheses.** Tool-use/result identity, Anthropic streaming conversion, request-scoped agent availability, cycle handling and screenshot-envelope compatibility are particular to this implementation. H0132’s inspected intermediate request actually omitted instruction and image content and was revised; that does not show the final code retained the defect (events 49–57). Teacher concerns about global target lookup or incompatible envelopes are diagnoses or compatibility hypotheses, not established causes of unnamed formal failures (H0080 event 5; H0042 events 14–19). H0002’s and H0081’s five failed formal cases remain unidentified. No causal superiority of one approach or hint follows from differing scores.

**Coverage limits.** This batch contains software traces, not a Scene task: no scene construction, acceptance, or independently observed visual quality is evidenced; image data in H0132 was a mocked request, not a render assessment. Some inventories include usage ledgers, while older usage fields are blank; absence is not zero and old model cost cannot be recovered from it. The report is audit-only and does not generate solutions or feedback.
